headline: Spatial models couple influenza dispersal, defective particles and interferon signalling
label: Spatial Modelling Of Viral Infection
summary: Respiratory virus spread combines local expansion with long-range seeding, motivating spatially resolved models of within-host infection dynamics.
synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic modelling of viral infection within the host, where spatial structure and host innate responses are represented explicitly. The bridging-scales preprint distinguishes local expansion of respiratory viruses from occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. The spatially explicit stochastic influenza model extends this framing to in vitro infection, integrating defective interfering particles, type I interferon signalling and dispersal. The remaining items, an autophagy-targeting live attenuated influenza vaccine and heart-nosed bat alphacoronavirus entry via human CEACAM6, address vaccine design and zoonotic entry rather than spatial dynamics, so they share the topic only loosely. What is new is the explicit coupling of spatial dispersal with interferon feedback in a single stochastic framework.
